title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 193 (Contract by One Person Company)

content.overview: Section 193 provides that where a One Person Company limited by shares enters into a contract with the sole member of the company who is also its director, the company shall, unless the contract is in writing, ensure that the terms of the contract or offer are contained in a memorandum or are recorded in the minutes of the first meeting of the Board of Directors of the company held next after entering into the contract. The company shall inform the Registrar about every such contract within a period of fifteen days of the date of approval by the Board. The section does not apply to contracts entered into by the company in the ordinary course of its business.
content.glance: OPC contract with sole member who is also director: terms in writing, or in a memorandum, or recorded in minutes of next Board meeting; inform ROC within 15 days of Board approval; ordinary-course contracts excepted.

The company shall inform the Registrar about every contract entered into by the company and recorded in the minutes of the meeting of its Board of Directors under this section within a period of fifteen days of the date of approval by the Board of Directors. Nothing in this section shall apply to contracts entered into by the company in the ordinary course of its business. sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: One Person Company limited by shares contracting with its sole member who is also a director, other than in the ordinary course of business.

sections.heading: Form of Terms
sections.body: Contract in writing, or terms in a memorandum, or recorded in the minutes of the next Board meeting after the contract is entered into.

sections.heading: ROC Intimation
sections.body: Company informs the Registrar of every such contract recorded in Board minutes within fifteen days of Board approval.

sections.heading: Ordinary-Course Exception
sections.body: Contracts in the ordinary course of the company’s business are outside the section.

examples.title: OPC self-dealing recorded in minutes
examples.body: An OPC’s sole member-director sells equipment to the company outside the ordinary course. The terms are not in a signed contract but are recorded in the minutes of the next Board meeting, and the ROC is informed within 15 days. Section 193 is satisfied.

examples.title: Ordinary-course supply
examples.body: The same OPC regularly buys stationery from a shop owned by the sole member in the ordinary course at market rates. Section 193 does not apply to ordinary-course contracts.

hypotheticals.question: Must every OPC contract with its sole member be filed with the ROC?
hypotheticals.analysis: Only contracts that fall within s. 193 (sole member who is also director; not ordinary course) and that are recorded under the section need to be intimated to the Registrar within fifteen days of Board approval. Ordinary-course contracts are outside the section.

distinctions.title: OPC contract with sole member (s. 193) vs disclosure of interest (s. 184)
distinctions.left: Form and ROC intimation for OPC self-dealing contracts
distinctions.right: General director interest disclosure and non-participation

misconceptions.trap: OPC contracts with the sole member never need any formal record because there is only one person.
misconceptions.correction: Section 193 specifically requires writing, a memorandum, or recording in the next Board minutes (except ordinary-course contracts), plus ROC intimation where the section applies.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 193 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm OPC and sole member-director. II. Test ordinary-course exception. III. Require writing/memorandum/minutes. IV. Check 15-day ROC intimation. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: OPC facts; contract nature; form of record; ROC filing; precise relief.
